food: Drink a glass of water right after waking up, before coffee.
Prep breakfast the night before so mornings need zero decisions.
Protein first, carbs second — it keeps you full until lunch.
Keep a bag of nuts or fruit at your desk for when hunger hits before lunch.
Batch-cook eggs on Sunday — a boiled egg is breakfast in 10 seconds.
focus: Close every tab you're not using right now — fewer tabs, fewer decisions.
Write down tomorrow's first task before you log off today.
One notification check per hour beats twenty small interruptions.
Do the hardest task first, while your focus is freshest.
Stand up and stretch for 2 minutes every hour — it resets your attention.
gym: You don't have to feel motivated to start — motivation usually shows up after the first set.
A short session beats a skipped one. Show up, even for 20 minutes.
Progress isn't linear — a slower week doesn't erase the last one.
Pack your gym bag the night before so 19h has one less excuse.
Three years off doesn't reset to zero — your body remembers faster than you think.
reading: Two books a year is the goal — one page tonight is already ahead of schedule.
Getting lost in your own ideas while reading isn't a distraction, it's part of it.
A slow chapter on Saturday still counts as progress.
No need to finish in one sitting — put it down anywhere, pick it up anywhere.
